items.item_text: High school diploma, GED or equivalent work experience
Graduate of an accredited college with a bachelor’s degree, preferably in a health-related field
Basic experience in clinical or applied research
Previous experience in human subjects research and clinical trials
Experience working in a team environment
Work or volunteer experience in an Emergency Department setting
Ability to learn and use software and processes through coursework, training or previous work experience
Work or educational experience with blood/urine specimen processing and storage

The Assistant Clinical Research Coordinator (Assistant CRC) will work on clinical trials and other research studies in the Department of Emergency Medicine. The Assistant CRC will be involved in interdisciplinary studies focusing on research questions in Emergency Medicine for pediatric patients. The Assistant CRC is responsible for assisting more senior emergency medicine and Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN) CRC staff with aspects of the conduct of clinical studies, including: subject screening and recruitment, enrollment, scheduling, data collection, participant tracking, and regulatory support. Additional responsibilities may include assisting with general research coordination, clinical research enrollment and coordination, preparation for audits and monitor visits, study closeouts, training and other grant support. Work is performed under direction of the Principal Investigator, supervisor, and other senior staff. This position is funded by extramural grants and/or contracts.
70% - Clinical Research Coordination
10% - General Research Program Responsibilities
Completion of the Collaborative Institutional Training Initiative (CITI) Biomedical Researchers and Good Clinical Practice training programs
Computer skills sufficient to effectively use MS Word, Excel, web interfaces, patient or research databases, and electronic health record system
Basic knowledge of federal, state and university regulations for clinical research; ability to read, understand, and adhere to local and central Institutional Review Board policies and procedures
Basic knowledge of clinical research concepts and biomedical terminology

Ability to independently read and understand complex clinical research protocols with careful attention to detail; and to implement a broad range of activities as specified by clinical study protocols, as well as by University and departmental policies and procedures
Ability to explain and convey concepts
Excellent interpersonal skills demonstrating professionalism, compassion, and resourcefulness when interacting with a diverse population of patients
Demonstrated ability for self-directed learning

Demonstrate verbal and written communication skills to clearly and concisely provide information, explanations and instructions to, and elicit information from patients, patient’s families, physicians, hospital staff and a wide variety of health care professionals with varying levels of ability to understand
Ability to read and understand patient medical records, abstract clinical data and record accurately on case report forms and/or in electronic databases
Display organizational skills to coordinate multiple tasks, to appropriately prioritize workload, and to maintain research records
Basic knowledge of anatomy, physiology, medical terminology and procedures to effectively interpret and accurately compile data according to study protocol
Advanced-level knowledge of basic anatomy, medical terminology, and ability to interpret physicians’ notes, medical records, and laboratory and scan results
